'''Solaran Education''' refers to the modern school and literacy system of [[Solara]], especially the system shaped by the [[Education Reform Act of 1895]] and the adoption of the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] alphabet.

== Literacy Model ==

Solaran education separated mass literacy from elite classical training. Most students learned the [[Solaran Language]] through Sunline first, giving them access to newspapers, public notices, contracts, schoolbooks, and government information.

[[Solra]], the Elder Tongue, remained important but was taught later and more selectively. Its study belonged to priestly, legal, archival, scholarly, and high administrative tracks.

== Reform Period ==

The 1895 reform launched a three-year testing period for Sunline in schools, followed by official adoption in 1898.

After adoption, the [[Solaran Ministry of Education]] guided curriculum implementation, the [[Solaran Language Office]] supported official standards, and the [[Solaran Academy of Linguistics]] supplied post-adoption study from its 1900 source reference.

The reform made education a major instrument of Solaran national integration. A shared alphabet allowed teachers, ministries, publishers, and local officials to operate in a common written standard.

The reform period also overlaps with the first source-backed modern Solaran literary figure. [[Jane Pensworth]] began writing [[A Wild World]] in 1897, during the Sunline testing period, and the first book was published in 1901.

== Political Importance ==

By the twentieth century, Solaran education helped reinforce the state's sense of unity and modernity. It gave Solara a literate public sphere while allowing older ceremonial institutions to retain prestige.

This balance mattered in Solaran political culture: the country could present itself as both ancient and modern, ceremonial and parliamentary, traditional and industrial.

== Canon Notes ==

The source references later curriculum standards after 1994. This draft uses the pre-1994 literacy structure and reform history but avoids later school policy as fixed 1994 canon.
